transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Carva Coleman.
President Trump will campaign in Alaska today for incumbent Republican Senator Dan Sullivan.
Trump's been stumping mostly in red states, and that included last night in Ohio.
He told rallygoers the war against Iran will soon conclude.
It's going to end very soon, and as soon as it ends, your gasoline comes down.
But remember, your prices, your gas prices are lower than when Biden was president, and
he didn't do anything about Iran, the Islamic Republic of Iran.
AAA says the price of regular gas in the U.S. hit an all-time high in June 2022 when Joe
Biden was president.
At that time, it was more than $5 a gallon.
Meanwhile, AAA also says the cost of diesel hit an all-time high last month at nearly
$6.53 a gallon, largely because of the war with Iran.
Bulgarian Prime Minister Roman Rodov is summoning Russia's ambassador.
This follows drone strikes on ships in the Black Sea.
Esmi Nicholson has more.
Rodov says two ships have been struck off the coast of Bulgaria in drone attacks just
a week after a similar incident sank a vessel in the same area.
European Commission President Uzala Fonda Line has condemned the attacks, describing
the Black Sea as another front in Russia's war in Ukraine.
Cargo ships in the Black Sea transport grain from Ukraine, and the shipping route is a
lifeline for global food security.
Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sebya says Russia is weaponizing hunger to hold the world
hostage and urged Ukraine's partners to increase pressure on Moscow.
For NPR News, I'm Esmi Nicholson in Berlin.
NATO's Supreme Allied commander says the Western military alliance is prepared to fight immediately
if it is attacked.
U.S. General Alexis Grinkovich says if Russia decides to attack Europe, NATO will respond
with troops and autonomous systems to stop it.
He spoke at the Warsaw Security Forum.
A new survey finds more than 80 percent of Gen Z'ers believe skilled trades offer better
long-term job security than many office jobs.
And Piers Windsor Johnston reports some young people say AI is playing a role in their career
choices.
30 percent of Gen Z respondents in the survey by thumbtack say AI has made them more interested
in the trades.
Co-founder and CEO Marco Zappacosta says many of them are thinking beyond their first job.
Young people are thinking about which careers to get into, but I think security is kind
of top of the list when people are thinking about where to invest their time and ultimately
their years of their career.
Zappacosta says some tradespeople are using AI for tasks like invoicing and customer
follow-ups, but hands-on work still requires a person.
Federal projections show electrical and plumbing jobs growing through 2035, while AI and automation
will help reduce demand for some office jobs.
Windsor Johnston, NPR News.
It's NPR.
Minnesota Democratic Congresswoman Ilhan Omar says the Trump administration is politically
targeting her.
Omar's home in Washington, D.C., was searched yesterday by federal agents.
The Justice Department says that search is part of an ongoing federal investigation.
Omar and President Trump have often verbally sparred.
New York City's Mayor Zoran Mamdani says he is ordering a comprehensive review of the
city police department's use of force practices.
And Pierre's Michelle Aslim reports on the first such review in a decade.
The review of the NYPD's use of force practices comes after complaints that an officer involved
in a fatal shooting in 2024 was able to retire before he faced disciplinary proceedings.
In a statement, the mayor said the review is about making sure New Yorkers and their
families can trust their city will treat them with "care and dignity."
The Mamdani administration also announced it will increase funding for the Office of
the Inspector General in order to strengthen independent oversight.
The union, representing many of NYPD's officers, released a statement pushing back on the mayor's
efforts and said they "won't make New Yorkers any safer."
Michelle Aslim, NPR News.
Actor and disability rights champion RJ Mitty has died at the age of 34.
That's according to his representatives.
Mitty had cerebral palsy, but his cause of death has not been disclosed.
He was famous for his essential role on the show Breaking Bad.
He played Walter White Jr., the son of actor Bryan Cranston's teacher, turned meth dealer.
It's NPR.
Want to hear this podcast without sponsor breaks?

Or you can also support NPR's vital journalism and get NPR+ at plus.npr.org.
That's plus.npr.org.
